newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in quiet trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in late trading on Monday, with some pressure seen on swap rates, dealers said.
They said overall trading was very quiet, with players seen staying mainly on the sidelines.
"There is barely any volume. We just go with the market. We do not really want to do much," one U.S. bank dealer said.
"We have enough profits for this year," another said.
Dealers said they would prefer to stay on the sidelines unless something really fundamental happened.
Spot rupiah was at 2,337.0/37.2 at 0830 GMT against an opening of 2,336.5/37.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,336.5/37.0 and 2,336.25/36.5, respectively.
Dealers said a higher central bank fixing did not surprise the market as it had been widely anticipated.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,337/2,529 and the conversion rate to 2,337/2,385 on Monday.
The central bank has depreciated the rupiah by 16 points in the past five weeks.
One Japanese bank dealer said the higher fixing and ample rupiah supply did not affect sentiment on the local currency.
The U.S. bank dealer said ample liquidity seemed to put some pressure on the swap market, especially in three-month swap which eased to 48 points.
He said operators were also anticipating some declines of domestic interest rates next year which seemed to have extended pressure on longer-term swap rates.
Overnight money was last at 9.5 percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.30/0.35 and tom/next at 0.35/0.39.
One-month swap was at 15.00/15.25, two at 32.0/33.0, three at 47.5/48.0 and six at 92.0/94.0 points.
